title: 10 Best Event Analytics Platforms for B2B Event Teams | Zuddl Blog
summary: Compare 10 event analytics platforms on CRM sync depth, revenue attribution, and portfolio reporting. Each entry covers strengths, gaps, pricing, and best fit
body_markdown:
‍


Your flagship conference ended three days ago. The CMO wants pipeline numbers. The sales VP wants to know which attendees are worth calling first. You open your event platform and find aggregate attendance counts, a handful of pie charts, and no connection to the CRM records that would make any of it actionable. The data exists somewhere, but not in a form anyone can use before the moment passes.


Event analytics platforms manage more than dashboards and charts. They sit at the intersection of event operations, revenue operations, and executive reporting. The right platform captures per-attendee behavioral data, connects it to CRM opportunity records, and surfaces program-level comparisons that let finance teams evaluate events as a managed investment rather than a cost line item.


This article evaluates 10 event analytics platforms across CRM integration depth, revenue and pipeline attribution, and portfolio-level reporting across event types. Each entry covers what the platform does well for B2B event teams, where it has gaps, pricing, and the specific team situation it fits best.

## The 10 best event analytics platforms for B2B event teams


### Zuddl


Zuddl is an AI-native unified events platform that provides dedicated pre-event, live, and post-event analytics dashboards across conferences, field events, and webinars from a single interface. It serves B2B teams that need event data connected directly to CRM opportunity records without manual assembly.


**What it does well:**


- [Bidirectional real-time sync with Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, and Eloqua](https://www.zuddl.com/event-integrations) passes detailed registrant statuses (invited, registration abandoned, approved, rejected, registered, attended) directly into CRM, so sales reps work from current data rather than stale batch exports.
- [Revenue and pipeline attribution dashboard](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-analytics) tracks pipeline influenced, revenue generated, and key account movement at both the individual event and program level, giving event teams a direct answer when finance asks what the event budget produced.
- Unified data layer across conferences, field events, and webinars means series-level analytics aggregate roadshow impact across multiple city events, and program dashboards compare ROI across event types without manually combining CSVs.
- Per-attendee engagement analytics capture poll responses, Q&A submissions, watch time, and CTA clicks as granular behavioral data, enabling sales teams to distinguish a 45-minute engaged attendee from a five-minute drop-in before making outreach calls.
- Clean, structured report exports can be shared with sales VPs and executives who do not have platform access, without requiring the event team to manually reformat data into slide decks.


**Where it has gaps:**


- Building custom dashboards or cross-event comparison views requires time investment and occasionally support involvement, particularly for first-time users configuring advanced analytics.
- CRM field mapping between Zuddl engagement data and CRM objects (especially custom fields) requires configuration work upfront, and sync errors during initial setup are not always surfaced clearly.


**Pricing:** Digital plan starting at $10,000/year (2 organizers); Unified plan starting at $12,000/year.[See pricing](https://www.zuddl.com/pricing)


**Ratings:** 4.8/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B event teams replacing a fragmented stack of separate tools for conferences, field events, and webinars who need bidirectional CRM sync, pipeline attribution tied to opportunity records, and cross-event-type ROI comparison in a single platform without manual data stitching.


### Goldcast


Goldcast captures 21 distinct engagement data points per attendee across webinars and virtual events, making it one of the deeper sources of per-attendee behavioral data for sales teams prioritizing post-event outreach. It serves B2B marketing teams running digital-first event programs where engagement scoring drives lead qualification.


**What it does well:**


- Tracks 20+ distinct activity triggers per event, including watch time, poll responses, Q&A interactions, and CTA clicks, compiled into an engagement analytics dashboard that sales teams use to rank post-event outreach targets.
- Native integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Eloqua, and Pardot automatically sync registration and attendance data into CRM records with minimal manual intervention.
- AI Event Analyst provides automated post-event insights including attendee volume, watch time, engagement scores, and benchmark comparisons, reducing the time between event close and actionable analysis.


**Where it has gaps:**


- Post-event analytics are fully updated two hours after the event ends, which means live operational dashboards during the event itself are not available for mid-event corrections.
- Portfolio-level cross-event reporting is a documented gap. Aggregating analytics across multiple events or event types in a single view requires manual data exports per reviewer feedback.
- CRM sync monitoring and error visibility are limited. When integration syncs fail or data is missing in CRM, there is limited tooling to diagnose and retry failed records.
- No native pipeline or revenue attribution dashboard connects event attendance to CRM opportunity records. Linking engagement data to deal progression requires manual stitching.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.7/5 on G2 · Not available on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B marketing teams running webinar-heavy and virtual event programs who need deep per-attendee engagement data (21 data points per user) flowing into CRM for sales prioritization, and who can tolerate gaps in live dashboards and portfolio-level reporting.


### Bizzabo


Bizzabo provides a centralized analytics dashboard with real-time updates covering check-ins, session attendance, ratings, and mobile app adoption across in-person, virtual, and hybrid events. It serves mid-to-large B2B event teams managing multi-format programs with a need for engagement data that feeds CRM and marketing automation workflows.


**What it does well:**


- Real-time session attendance tracking during hybrid events gives on-site teams live visibility into attendee movement and session fill through mobile app integration.
- Klik SmartBadge wearables capture in-person behavioral data (booth visits, session attendance, networking interactions) that is not available on competing platforms, adding a layer of engagement intelligence beyond digital signals.
- Native integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Pardot, and Eloqua push registration and attendance data into CRM records, reducing manual data entry for post-event lead nurturing.
- On-demand content analytics for virtual events track engagement from first registration to final replay, providing content performance signals that extend beyond the live event window.


**Where it has gaps:**


- Connecting event attendance directly to CRM opportunity records for pipeline attribution requires manual effort or external BI tools. Out-of-the-box revenue attribution reporting is not granular enough for deal-level analysis.
- Cross-event portfolio-level reporting requires manual data exports and stitching in external tools. Normalizing metrics across different event types (conferences vs. webinars vs. field events) is not natively supported in a unified dashboard.
- Bidirectional sync (CRM context flowing back into Bizzabo) is inconsistent and often requires custom API work, especially for field-level mapping between CRM objects and event data.
- Scheduled or automated report delivery to stakeholders is limited, often requiring manual intervention to share data with non-platform users.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.3/5 on G2 · 4.4/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B event teams running large in-person conferences and hybrid programs who need session-level and wearable-based engagement data flowing into established CRM workflows, and who have the internal resources to configure integrations and manage manual portfolio reporting.


### Cvent Event Management


Cvent offers enterprise-grade reporting that links attendee engagement data to business outcomes such as pipeline and revenue, with centralized analytics across one flagship conference or hundreds of field events. It serves large enterprise organizations managing high-volume event portfolios where standardized processes and Salesforce integration maturity are priorities.


**What it does well:**


- CventIQ Instant Session Insights uses AI to analyze audience comments for sentiment, speaker performance, session content engagement, and logistics feedback, providing session-level content analytics beyond basic attendance counts.
- Cvent Access Portal gives non-Cvent users real-time event data and reporting without requiring a full platform license, addressing the stakeholder access problem directly.
- AI-powered insights summarize performance trends and highlight what drove results, making it easier to communicate impact to executive stakeholders who do not use the platform.


**Where it has gaps:**


- Real-time live-event operational dashboards are a gap per reviewer consensus. Standard dashboards lack the modern, at-a-glance operational view newer platforms offer, and live operational views require add-on products.
- CRM integration setup, field mapping, and sync configuration require significant IT involvement and professional services hours, often delaying go-live by weeks.
- Cross-event-type normalized comparison (conferences vs. webinars vs. field dinners in one view) is not explicitly claimed on vendor pages, and advanced analytics features are often gated behind higher-tier modules.
- No explicit UTM parameter tracking or multi-channel campaign attribution is documented on reviewed product pages.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.3/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Enterprise organizations managing dozens or hundreds of annual events who need a mature Salesforce integration, AI-driven session insights, and stakeholder access portals, and who have the IT resources and budget to handle complex configuration and module-based pricing.


### Swoogo


Swoogo provides event dashboards, cross-event reporting, and a global attendee record that lets teams slice data across multiple events without per-event or per-registrant charges. It serves B2B event teams running multi-city series or roadshows who need to compare performance across events without rebuilding reports from scratch each time.


**What it does well:**


- Cross-event reporting and the global attendee record are cited by reviewers as differentiating features, allowing teams to compare a 12-city roadshow series in a single reporting view without manually exporting and combining CSVs from each event.
- Full REST API with 140+ endpoints supports custom integrations with CRM and marketing automation tools, giving technical teams flexibility to build workflows beyond native connectors.
- Unlimited events and unlimited registrants on all plans eliminate the per-event cost calculations that make budget planning unpredictable on other platforms.


**Where it has gaps:**


- Pipeline and revenue attribution requires connecting Swoogo data to an external BI tool or CRM. Swoogo itself does not close the attribution loop to opportunity records per reviewer feedback.
- Bidirectional CRM sync is limited. Data flows from Swoogo to CRM, but CRM account context does not automatically enrich event workflows. Sync monitoring and error logging are not surfaced clearly in the UI.
- Cross-event-type comparisons (comparing webinar pipeline vs. field event pipeline) are not natively normalized and require manual effort.
- Stakeholders without Swoogo logins cannot access live dashboards. Reporting still requires exporting and emailing files.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.8/5 on G2 · 4.8/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B event teams running multi-city roadshows or repeating event series who need cross-event reporting and a global attendee record without per-event charges, and whose revenue attribution needs can be handled by connecting Swoogo data to external BI or CRM tools.


### SpotMe


SpotMe claims native two-way CRM integration with Salesforce, Veeva, Marketo, and HubSpot, and provides real-time measurement of session engagement, drop-off rates, and speaker performance. It serves enterprise teams in regulated industries (pharma, life sciences, financial services) running high-touch in-person and hybrid events.


**What it does well:**


- Session-level analytics measure engagement, drop-off rates, and speaker performance in real time, giving content teams signals on what held attention versus what caused audience exit.
- Per-attendee behavioral signals from live polling, word clouds, sentiment analysis, gamification (challenges, leaderboards, rewards), and AI-powered matchmaking generate granular engagement data that CRM integration claims suggest flows to connected systems.
- Veeva CRM integration is a rare capability relevant to pharmaceutical and life sciences event teams who need compliance-aware data flows between event engagement and regulated CRM systems.


**Where it has gaps:**


- No pipeline or revenue attribution dashboard is documented on public vendor pages. Connecting event attendance to CRM opportunity records or deal progression is not a confirmed native capability.
- Exporting analytics for stakeholder sharing requires additional manual steps. Shareable dashboard links for non-platform users are not consistently available per reviewer feedback.
- Cross-event portfolio reporting is claimed by the vendor but reviewers report difficulty aggregating data across multiple events or event types without manual data work.
- Integration configuration and analytics mapping require significant implementation time and vendor support involvement.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.6/5 on G2 · 4.5/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Enterprise pharma, life sciences, and financial services teams running high-compliance in-person events who need Veeva integration, session-level drop-off analytics, and rich attendee engagement capture, and who have implementation resources for a platform that requires vendor-supported configuration.


### Splash


Splash provides automatic analytics dashboards showing metrics by event, email campaign, ticket payout, and page traffic, with integrations to Salesforce, Marketo, HubSpot, and Slack. It serves marketing teams running branded field events and experiential programs where registration design and check-in operations are the primary workflow.


**What it does well:**


- CRM integrations with Salesforce, Marketo, HubSpot, and Slack push registration data in real time, reducing manual data entry after events. Support SLAs are available for complex integration configurations.
- Guest-list management with custom tags, filtering by registration status, and segmented follow-ups gives marketing teams post-event targeting capability tied directly to attendance data.
- Mobile check-in app provides real-time visibility into door arrivals, allowing on-site teams to monitor guest arrival counts as they happen.


**Where it has gaps:**


- CRM sync is primarily one-directional. Data flows to CRM, but CRM context does not flow back into Splash. No native integration monitoring or retry logs are available per reviewer feedback.
- No native pipeline or revenue attribution dashboard links attendance to CRM opportunity progression. Proving pipeline impact requires exporting data and manually connecting it to opportunity records.
- Session-level analytics are not available. Analytics stop at the event level without session-specific attendance, drop-off, or content performance data.
- Program-level portfolio reporting lacks cross-event-type normalization. Comparing ROI across webinars, field events, and conferences requires manual CSV exports and external spreadsheet work.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.4/5 on G2 · 4.4/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** B2B marketing teams running branded field events and experiential activations who prioritize event page design, registration workflow, and on-site check-in operations, and whose analytics needs are limited to event-level registration and attendance reporting with CRM push.


### RainFocus


RainFocus provides real-time analytics and reporting on event performance and participant behavior, with native Salesforce and Marketo integration and support for in-person, virtual, and hybrid programs from one platform. It serves large enterprises managing complex, high-volume event programs that require dedicated implementation resources.


**What it does well:**


- Real-time analytics with native visualization tools surface trends during events, and behavioral data tracking spans the full event lifecycle from registration through post-event follow-up.
- Global attendee profiles consolidate participant data across event formats, supporting personalization that carries forward from one event to the next.
- Enterprise-scale program management from a single system is a frequently cited advantage for organizations running dozens or hundreds of events annually.


**Where it has gaps:**


- No explicit UTM parameter tracking or campaign source attribution capability is documented on vendor product pages.
- Reporting and dashboard customization can be rigid. Building custom reports or extracting specific data cuts often requires support from the RainFocus team rather than self-service configuration.
- No pipeline or revenue attribution dashboard connecting event attendance to CRM opportunity records is documented on public pages.
- No shareable reports, scheduled exports, or stakeholder-accessible dashboards for non-platform users are explicitly claimed.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.5/5 on G2 · Not available on Capterra


**Best for:** Large enterprise organizations managing complex, multi-format event programs at scale who have dedicated implementation teams and technical resources, and who prioritize real-time behavioral analytics and unified attendee profiles over self-serve reporting or transparent pricing.


### Webex Events


Webex Events (formerly Socio) provides post-event analytics covering registrations, attendance counts, and session participation, with check-in and badge scan data exportable to CRM. It serves teams already operating within the Cisco ecosystem who need basic event analytics with live check-in visibility for hybrid events.


**What it does well:**


- Real-time check-in visibility during in-person events shows live badge scan counts through the mobile check-in app, giving on-site coordinators immediate awareness of door arrivals.
- Post-event session attendance reports are downloadable, showing which sessions were attended and by whom, with Q&A and polling data captured at the session level and exportable for content review.
- Sponsor lead retrieval tools capture booth scan data and allow reps to add per-attendee notes, providing a proxy for sponsorship value reporting.


**Where it has gaps:**


- CRM sync is largely one-directional and manual. Data must be exported and imported rather than syncing in real time. Bidirectional sync (CRM account context flowing back into the platform) is not confirmed by reviewers.
- Cross-event analytics do not exist natively. Each event's data lives in its own silo. Comparing city-by-city performance in a roadshow requires downloading separate CSVs and reconciling them in spreadsheets.
- Per-attendee behavioral profiles (watch time, session sequence, CTA clicks, resource downloads) are not consolidated into a single view. Engagement data arrives as flat export files requiring manual transformation before it can feed lead scoring models.
- No native pipeline or revenue attribution dashboard is described by reviewers or confirmed by vendor data.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.4/5 on G2 · 4.4/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Teams operating within the Cisco ecosystem who need basic post-event session and attendance analytics with live check-in counting, and whose pipeline attribution and cross-event reporting needs are handled by external BI tools or CRM-native reports.


### Whova


Whova generates post-event analytics reports that run over 60 pages, covering engagement, networking, marketing performance, session attendance, sponsor impressions, and logistics. It serves association and conference organizers who need detailed single-event reporting and attendee engagement data without building dashboards from scratch.


**What it does well:**


- Real-time analytics with live stats dynamically update during events, tracking app downloads, sponsor banner views, check-in progress, survey responses, and overall activity, allowing on-the-spot decisions about room capacity and attendance pacing.
- AI-Generated Event Summary provides organizers with a detailed, written overview of event achievements that can be shared with leadership without requiring manual narrative assembly.
- Session attendance tracking and engagement data (polls, Q&A, community board activity) give content teams clear signals on which sessions drew interest and which prompted attendee interaction.


**Where it has gaps:**


- CRM integration is a consistently cited limitation. Syncing attendee engagement detail into Salesforce or HubSpot requires manual exports rather than automated bidirectional sync.
- No cross-event or program-level portfolio reporting exists. Each event is a silo. Users must manually combine data to compare performance across a series or event types.
- UTM and campaign source attribution is not tracked through to registration. Reviewers report difficulty understanding which marketing channels drove sign-ups.
- Revenue and pipeline attribution to CRM opportunities is not supported natively. Connecting event attendance to deal records requires manual data work.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing; not listed publicly.


**Ratings:** 4.8/5 on G2 · 4.8/5 on Capterra


**Best for:** Association and conference organizers running large single events who need comprehensive post-event reports (60+ pages) and AI-generated summaries for stakeholder communication, and whose analytics needs do not extend to CRM pipeline attribution or cross-event portfolio comparison.


## What to look for in event analytics platforms for B2B event teams


**Campaign and registration source attribution:** Evaluate whether UTM parameters survive device switches and third-party redirects through to CRM records. If they do not, every registration shows as "direct" and you cannot determine which promotion channels justify continued investment.


**CRM integration depth, bidirectional sync, and monitoring:** Test whether event data flows to CRM in real time and whether CRM context (opportunity stage, account tier) flows back. Without bidirectional sync, sales reps operate on stale data and event teams cannot personalize experiences by account value.


**Live and real-time operational dashboards:** Confirm that dashboards update during the live event, not after it ends. Post-event-only analytics mean low session attendance and broken registration flows are discovered too late to correct.


**Session-level content performance analytics:** Check for per-session attendance, drop-off analysis, and engagement heatmaps for on-demand content. Without this granularity, content and programming decisions for future events rely on gut feel rather than data.


**Attendee-level engagement analytics and lead scoring enrichment:** Verify that per-attendee behavioral data (watch time, poll responses, Q&A questions, CTA clicks) flows into CRM as discrete, mappable fields. A binary "attended: yes/no" flag gives sales teams nothing to prioritize with.


**Pipeline and revenue attribution dashboard:** Look for native linkage between event attendance and CRM opportunity records. Without it, events remain a cost line item because no one can prove which deals attended which events or whether attendance correlated with deal progression.


**Shareable and stakeholder-accessible reporting.** Confirm that analytics can reach stakeholders (CFOs, sponsors, sales VPs) who do not have platform logins. If reports require manual reformatting into slide decks, the event team becomes a bottleneck between data and decisions.


**Program-level portfolio reporting across event types.** Evaluate whether the platform compares ROI across conferences, field events, and webinars in a single normalized view. Without cross-event-type comparison, budget allocation decisions are made without knowing which format produces the most pipeline per dollar.


## Questions people ask about event analytics platforms


**What metrics should you track to measure event success?**


Track registration-to-attendance conversion, session-level attendance and drop-off, per-attendee engagement depth (poll responses, Q&A submissions, watch time), pipeline influenced, and revenue attributed to event attendance. Registration counts alone tell you volume. Pipeline and revenue attribution tell you whether the event budget produced business outcomes.


**What should event analytics software integrate with?**


At minimum, your CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot) and marketing automation platform (Marketo, Eloqua, Pardot). Bidirectional sync matters. One-directional push means event data reaches CRM but CRM context (opportunity stage, account tier) never reaches the event platform. Without that return flow, personalization and lead scoring enrichment are impossible.


**What is the difference between event analytics and event management software?**


Event management software handles logistics: registration, ticketing, check-in, agenda building, and attendee communication. Event analytics platforms go further by connecting attendee behavioral data to CRM records, attributing pipeline and revenue to specific events, and comparing ROI across an event portfolio. Many platforms claim both, but the analytics depth varies significantly.


**How can event analytics help improve ROI and attendee engagement?**


Event analytics improve ROI by connecting attendance data to CRM opportunity records so teams can prove which events influenced deals. They improve engagement by surfacing session-level drop-off and per-attendee behavioral signals, so content teams adjust programming based on data rather than assumptions. Zuddl's[pipeline and revenue attribution dashboards](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-analytics) tie event engagement directly to opportunity movement, removing the manual spreadsheet assembly that delays ROI reporting.
